account:
It is day 1, just after seven in the morning. I am at town hall with the secretary and builder. The secretary has given me the appointment book, which I have not yet read today; she says I have a mill inspection at ten. Builder wants a brief discussion about this week's maintenance inspection and payment terms. I have said that no repairs or payment are authorized, and that we should consult the appointments before scheduling him. This appears to be a request to arrange ordinary maintenance business, not evidence that repairs are actually needed.

The unusual matter is still a vague rumor of bridge or port changes. Yesterday our neighbour mentioned hearing it but supplied no source or specifics. The secretary traced another report through Townsfolk 03 to the innkeeper, who denied proposing or announcing any such change. Yesterday's accounts record reported no claims or receipts, no approved repair spending, and no established repair need. Builder reported the bridge passable, and relayed Freight's account of undamaged roads and a trouble-free ferry crossing. Those are reports, not my own inspections.

The secretary says our neighbour has offered to relay my request for a conversation to Townsfolk 03. I do not yet know that a meeting is arranged. I want to ask Townsfolk 03 exactly what was heard, from whom, and whether there is any concrete proposal. So far I have no evidence of a secret project or coordinated activity, and I cannot say what the rumor is for. It may be misunderstanding or ordinary gossip. My immediate business is to read today's appointment book, hear the builder without committing funds, and keep the ten o'clock mill inspection.
